correctness.rationale: For all three unit-circle nodes, Schur alternant factorization and the cubic discriminant give the exact polynomial F(r,u) with 0<=r<=3,-1<=u<=1. Strict quadratic concavity partitions the auxiliary maximum into F_-,F_0,F_+. Exact derivative factorization gives the unique root rho on (3/4,4/5), witness F_-(3/4)>22, and rational inequalities prove other branches <22. The symmetric triple attains the bound; unit-circle root polynomial gives every optimizer. Hadamard plus sums of cube roots establishes the tightness criterion. Symbolic exact polynomial identities and 62,453 supplementary numeric checks passed from the packaged checker; samples do not replace analytic proof.

value.rationale: For the natural three-mode scalar Fourier interpolation problem, the attainable determinant gives exact D-optimal sampling volume and its full geometrical optimizer. The first degree-two Schur factor case has a genuine angular/phase tradeoff and a strict nonorthogonality gap, not just a renamed ordinary Vandermonde extremizer or elementary Hadamard boundary; its explicit cubic and unique isosceles geometry provide a reproducible benchmark for sparse-order sampling. Does not claim a general all-spectra theorem.
